intro.name: The beginning
intro.text:
To celebrate the village's hardworking builders, farmers, and gatherers, the elders announce a friendly strength competition. Coconuts are stacked, water-filled clay jugs are carefully inspected, sturdy fallen logs are marked, and a large stone is placed at the edge of the clearing. (Strongman) volunteers. Several spectators immediately begin arguing about which feat should count as the greatest demonstration of strength.
WHAT CHALLENGE SHOULD (Strongman) ATTEMPT?

text_only.reason: narrative: 'celebrate' is part of the story, not a change the event makes

a1.text: The Walking Coconut Mountain: (Strongman) carries an astonishing number of coconuts across the finish line.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has a Physical skill

a2.text: The Clever Basket: (Strongman) uses a huge woven carrier and wins. The judges argue whether cleverness counts. The elders decide either to honor the feat or to introduce a separate ingenuity prize.

a3.text: The Great Coconut Avalanche: The stack tumbles harmlessly into the sand. Children race to collect the runaway coconuts while (Strongman) bows to the laughing crowd.

a4.text: The Patient Champion: A rival starts with more coconuts but drops them. (Strongman)'s slower, steadier effort wins the contest.

b1.text: Steady as Stone: (Strongman) holds two filled clay jugs longer than anyone else.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has a Physical skill

b2.text: The Unfortunate Splash: A cracked jug gives way, soaking (Strongman). The crowd roars with laughter; the organizers replace the jug and offer a fair retry.

b3.text: The Surprise Winner: A quiet villager with excellent balance defeats several boastful competitors. (Strongman) learns that control matters as much as brute force.

b4.text: A Sensible Withdrawal: (Strongman) notices a strained grip and stops before injury. No prize, but an elder praises good judgment.

text_only.reason: narrative: the contestant stops before any injury; nobody is hurt

c1.text: The Strongest on the Shore: (Strongman) moves the marked stone or fallen log farther than any competitor.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has a Physical skill

c2.text: The Leverage Lesson: A smaller competitor demonstrates a clever wooden lever. The judges award a separate prize for engineering;

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has a Physical skill

c3.text: Stuck in the Sand: The log sinks into soft sand. (Strongman) and a rival must work together to free it.

c4.text: The Overconfident Champion: (Strongman) boasts loudly, then cannot budge the load. A child remarks, "Perhaps your words were heavier."

d1.text: A Perfect Partnership: (Strongman) carries the volunteer steadily and wins. Both celebrate.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has a Physical skill

d2.text: The Talking Passenger: The volunteer offers nonstop advice about posture and foot placement. (Strongman) finishes but is thoroughly embarrassed; the audience is delighted.

d3.text: The Sudden Switch: The volunteer proves stronger than (Strongman) and jokingly offers to reverse roles. The crowd applauds.

d4.text: Teamwork Over Glory: (Strongman) decides the carry is unwise and helps organize a safer team challenge instead.

e1.text: The All-Around Champion: A balanced performance across coconut carrying, water-jug holding, and log moving earns the grand prize.

e2.text: Too Fast, Too Soon: (Strongman) exhausts (strongman.himself/herself) early and must rest; no injury, but an important lesson about pacing.
